## Summary
The weekend production check-in reviewed Sunday’s service, addressed minor technical issues, and aligned on adjustments for the upcoming weekend. The group agreed to push the live stream start to 9:25 AM, implement a dimmer preset for the opening lighting cue, and shelve the second confidence monitor until the January budget reset. Aaron will reprogram the lighting cue and track a delayed camera cable, while Speaker 2 will update the stream timer and rebuild the announcement slides.

## Decisions
- The live stream countdown will start at 9:25 AM moving forward.
- The second stage confidence monitor will be shelved until the budget resets in January.
- The opening of the service will use a programmed dimmer preset to fade house lights down and bring up the stage wash.

## Action items
- Speaker 2 — Update the ProPresenter countdown timer to 9:25.
- Speaker 2 — Rebuild the announcement slides from scratch and pull updated graphics from Hannah.
- Aaron — Reprogram the opening lighting cue (before Thursday rehearsal)
- Aaron — Check tracking for the new Camera 3 SDI cable and update the group chat (tonight)

## Open questions
- Whether the delayed Camera 3 SDI cable will arrive in time for Sunday and how to reposition the camera if it does not.

## Summary
The meeting focused on troubleshooting a flickering issue with the north lobby screen. After inspecting the equipment, they identified a loose and damaged HDMI cable as the likely cause and agreed to replace it. They also planned to upload a newly updated announcement loop and monitor the screen during Sunday’s live feed to confirm the issue is fully resolved.

## Decisions
- Replace the damaged HDMI cable connecting the media player to the north lobby screen.
- Upload the new announcement loop for Sunday services.
- Monitor the screen during the Sunday live feed to verify the flicker is gone before pursuing further repairs.
- Defer purchasing a new media player and addressing the dim hallway screen until a later date.

## Action items
- Aaron — Replace the damaged HDMI cable on the north lobby screen (before the weekend)
- Speaker 1 — Export the new announcement loop and copy it to the media player (this afternoon)
- Aaron and Speaker 1 — Monitor the north lobby screen during the live feed (Sunday)
- Speaker 1 — Research pricing for a modern media player for future reference (no deadline)

## Open questions
- Whether the hallway screen near the cafe needs a simple brightness adjustment or actual hardware repair.
- Long-term strategy for upgrading the aging north lobby media player and potentially the eight-year-old panel.

## Summary
Aaron contacted warranty support to report a failing lamp in the main worship center projector, which has been dimming, flickering, and triggering thermal shutdowns. Dana confirmed the unit is within its warranty window and initiated a replacement claim for the primary lamp. The team agreed to proceed with the warranty process, with Aaron temporarily switching the projector to eco mode to maintain service continuity.

## Decisions
- Proceed with a warranty claim for the primary projector lamp.
- Temporarily operate the projector in eco mode to reduce thermal load until the replacement arrives.

## Action items
- Aaron — Email the projector serial number and purchase receipt/invoice to warranty support (this afternoon)
- Dana — Validate the claim and email the RMA number and prepaid shipping label (by tomorrow)
- Marcus — Research warranty coverage for the second lamp module and follow up with Aaron
- Aaron — Run the projector in eco mode for the upcoming services

## Open questions
- Whether the second lamp module is covered under the same warranty window.
- Whether to eventually replace the entire projector with a newer laser unit (noted as a future consideration pending finance team approval).

## Summary
The team finalized the November camera volunteer schedule and addressed stream graphics staffing. After reviewing volunteer availability, they decided to run two manned cameras per service with the wide camera locked off to prevent burnout. Camera sign-ups will be handled through Planning Center, while Tyler will manage the separate graphics schedule. The group also flagged Thanksgiving weekend staffing as a pending item.

## Decisions
- November will use two manned cameras per service (center close and side), with the wide camera locked off on a looser preset framing.
- Camera volunteer scheduling will use Planning Center for self-serve sign-ups.
- Stream graphics scheduling will be managed separately by Tyler and will not be included in the Planning Center sign-ups.

## Action items
- Aaron — Build the draft camera schedule template in Planning Center (Friday)
- Dana — Nudge regular volunteers to claim camera slots once sign-ups open
- Tyler — Text Marcus to schedule a shadow weekend for graphics training
- Tyler — Build and manage the November stream graphics schedule
- Aaron — Ask the worship team about the service plan and staffing for Thanksgiving weekend

## Open questions
- What is the confirmed service schedule and volunteer availability for Thanksgiving weekend?

## Summary
This was a weekly MSP status call reviewing IT infrastructure, recent patching, and ongoing support tickets. The discussion focused on troubleshooting a failing overnight media NAS backup, addressing a flaky booth switch that drops signals during services, and preparing documentation for the church elders. The call concluded with clear troubleshooting steps for the network switch, a Monday deadline for the patch report, and a mutual agreement to defer the cloud migration proposal.

## Decisions
- Parked the cloud storage migration proposal for a future discussion.

## Action items
- Aaron — Power cycle the booth switch tonight and monitor it through Wednesday rehearsal.
- Devin — Investigate the overnight media NAS backup failure and verify the last successful backup copy.
- Devin — Email a patching summary report to Aaron (Monday).
- Aaron — Contact the LED wall vendor directly regarding the dead tile section.

## Open questions
- What is causing the scheduled media NAS backup to hang and fail at 2 AM?
- Will the booth switch continue dropping intercom and camera signals after the power cycle?

## Summary
The AVL team held a weekend production check-in to review last Sunday’s service and plan for the upcoming weekend. They addressed technical hiccups with ProPresenter and agreed to streamline the live stream countdown, rebuild outdated announcement slides, and program a new lighting preset for the service opener. Budget constraints led the group to postpone adding a second stage confidence monitor until January, and they noted a potential shipping delay for a replacement camera cable that remains unresolved.

## Decisions
- Push the live stream countdown start time to 9:25 AM.
- Rebuild the announcement slides from scratch to remove outdated event information.
- Implement a dimmer preset for the opening song to lower house lights and raise the stage wash.
- Postpone adding a second stage confidence monitor due to budget constraints, with plans to revisit in January.
- Park the proposal to switch the band to in-ear monitors until next year's gear budget discussion.

## Action items
- Speaker 2 — Update the ProPresenter countdown timer to 9:25 AM
- Speaker 2 — Rebuild the announcement slides and coordinate updated graphics with Hannah (this week)
- Aaron — Reprogram the opening lighting cue and test it live (before Thursday rehearsal)
- Aaron — Check tracking for the new Camera 3 SDI cable and update the group thread (tonight)

## Open questions
- Whether the new Camera 3 SDI cable will arrive in time for Sunday services.
- Where to position Camera 3 if the cable does not arrive and the existing backup run is too short to reach the back stage position.

## Summary
Aaron called warranty support to report a failing lamp on the main worship center projector (PX-9140), which has been dimming, flickering, and triggering thermal shutdowns. The support team confirmed the unit is still under warranty and agreed to process a replacement claim once proof of purchase and the serial number are provided. ## Summary
The meeting focused on finalizing the November camera volunteer schedule and stream graphics staffing. After reviewing volunteer availability, the group agreed to reduce manned cameras from three to two per service and lock off the wide shot to prevent volunteer burnout. They also established a self-serve Planning Center sign-up for cameras, assigned Tyler to independently manage graphics, and parked the Thanksgiving weekend staffing question for later.

## Decisions

- The wide camera will use a looser preset framing to cover stage resets like communion or baptisms.
- Camera volunteer scheduling will use a self-serve Planning Center sign-up rather than direct outreach.
- Tyler will independently manage the stream graphics schedule for November, separate from the camera sign-ups.

## Summary
This weekly MSP status call reviewed system backup health, weekend patching progress, and a flaky network switch in the production booth. The team parked a cloud migration discussion, confirmed most endpoints are patched, and aligned on troubleshooting steps for a recurring overnight NAS backup failure. The call concluded with Devin committing to a patch report by Monday and Aaron scheduled to reboot the switch tonight.

## Decisions
- Park the cloud migration discussion for a later date.
- Troubleshoot the flaky booth switch by having Aaron power cycle it tonight and Devin review port configurations if drops persist.
- Confirm that the Ultra Ex router and LED wall tile issue fall outside the MSP contract scope and will be handled by Aaron or the AV vendor.

## Action items
- Aaron — Power cycle the booth switch tonight and monitor stability through Wednesday rehearsal.
- Devin — Verify the most recent successful media NAS backup and investigate why the 2 AM scheduled job consistently fails.
- Devin — Complete remaining workstation patch checks and email a summary report clarifying MSP scope versus AV vendor scope to Aaron by Monday.

## Open questions
- What is causing the media NAS backup job to fail specifically during the overnight scheduled run?
- Will the power cycle resolve the booth switch drops, or will port configuration changes be required?
